pg_tables: public.billing_events (backyard-owned; upstream of the CDC mirror only -- Clarity never queries Postgres on this route)
data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: All three are PeerDB CDC mirrors, PRIMARY KEY id, ORDER BY id. zod.public_billing_events is ReplacingMergeTree(_peerdb_version) with NO _peerdb_is_deleted merge argument -- so tombstones do not auto-collapse at merge and the _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 filter is correctness-required, even though raw and FINAL counts are currently identical (38.0M both ways, so FINAL itself buys nothing and costs real time). zod.public_api_keys (4,140 rows) and zod.public_orgs (726,869 rows) ARE ReplacingMergeTree(_peerdb_version, _peerdb_is_deleted) and are small enough that FINAL + not-deleted is cheap and correct. Matches okf PG-002. Unlike DEV-2464's hotlist leg there is no drift concern: billing_events rows are immutable once written, so repeated readings do not move.
data_impact.indexes_relied_on: NONE usable. All three tables are ORDER BY id only, so org_id, api_key_id, event_type, ts and vin are all absent from every sort key and no primary-index pruning is available for any predicate this query needs. Measured consequence: read_rows is ~39.95M -- the whole table -- regardless of window width. The org-scoping and time-window predicates reduce only the SURVIVING row count, not the scan. This is the mechanical reason the caching rule is load-bearing and the reason a wider sparkline span is free.

resource_envelope.trigger: A new app/Clickhouse/Queries/* class reading a 38M-row production CDC mirror with no usable sort-key pruning, driven from a Filament dashboard widget rendered on every Company Metrics page load.

driving_tables.prod_rows_basis: prod-cardinality.sh 2026-09-08; raw == FINAL + not-deleted (no soft-deletes exist on this table yet)
driving_tables.group_by_note: That 23.1M group (api_key_id 4142, ~61% of the table) spans ALL event types, not case-claim. For the metric's own axis the worst case is far smaller: ranked by deduped claims counted on either side, Jul 2026, org 165 = 7,230 and the runner-up is 2,696. Candidate 3 correctly challenged the carried assumption that org 165 was the worst case; the driver re-measured and it holds by a factor of 2.7.

resource_envelope.growth: billing_events is append-only and grows across all event types (38.0M total against ~365K lifetime case-claim events, so case-claim is under 1% of it). Because nothing prunes, this query's scan cost tracks TOTAL table size, not case-claim selectivity -- so it grows with all billing activity, not just with this metric's own volume. That is the growth curve to watch. Carrying the repo's standing PG-027 caution against sizing to today's maximum.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Not a scheduled command or job, so there is no accumulation risk. PHP-side allocation is O(1): one integer plus a <=13-element monthly series, no per-row loop -- this card cannot reproduce the DEV-2342 host-memory failure mode. CORRECTED (review rounds 1-2, all three lanes): the earlier claim that cost is 'bounded by Cache::flexible([3600,86400]) to at most one fresh compute per (org, window) per hour' was WRONG for half this card. It holds ONLY for the monthly/sparkline seam (getMonthlyData -> heldFlexible). The today/last_7d seam goes through the base DashboardWidget::currentPeriodTotal() -> cache()->remember(..., getCacheTTL()) = 10 MINUTES (60s floor under admin_impersonator), so it runs up to 6 fresh ~40M-row computes per hour per org, not one. Operator decision 2026-09-08: leave that seam on the base class's caching, shared with the nine sibling cards, rather than adding a fifth override. FURTHER, also unstated before: a COLD today/last_7d render issues TWO independent ~40M-row scans, not one -- the window seam (getCardTotal -> currentPeriodTotal -> window()) AND the sparkline seam (chartSeries -> getMonthlyData -> monthlySeries). So ~80M read_rows and ~3.7GB for one cold page load on those two filter states. The one-cached-query AC is satisfied per SEAM, which is how the doubling went unrecorded. SERVER-SIDE MEASURED (via the X-ClickHouse-Summary header -- see below): read_rows 39,952,007 and peak memory_usage 437-489 MB, both essentially invariant across 1-, 3- and 13-month spans. Wall clock spans 0.3s to 9.3s across two sessions depending on shared-Cloud contention, well inside CLICKHOUSE_TIMEOUT_QUERY = 60s.
resource_envelope.envelope_method_note: DEV-2464 recorded the server-side envelope as UNOBTAINABLE because readonly_user lacks READ ON REMOTE, which denies clusterAllReplicas(system.query_log).
